map.保鲜液用量 = 花瓶水量 × 商用保鲜剂推荐浓度（可利鲜通常 1 包配 500: Preservative amount = vase water × commercial preservative recommended concentration (Chrysal usually 1 packet per 500 mL to 1 L water); homemade recipe per liter of water adds white sugar 10-20 g (nutrients) + white vinegar or citric acid 1-2 mL (acidify and inhibit bacteria, pH 3.5-4.5) + bleach 0.1-0.2 mL (disinfect); change the solution every 2-3 days and re-cut stems diagonally 1-2 cm to reopen water uptake, extending vase life by 30%-50%.
map.没有专业保鲜液时，可用家中常见材料自制: When no professional preservative is available, make one from common household materials
map.💡 自制保鲜液原理：糖分提供营养（相当于花蜜），白醋/柠檬酸抑制细菌，漂白剂杀菌: 💡 Homemade preservative principle: sugar provides nutrition (like nectar), white vinegar/citric acid inhibits bacteria, bleach kills bacteria. Change the preservative every 2-3 days and re-cut stems diagonally.

map.可复现算例：500ml 水两种方案: Reproducible example: 500 ml water, two plans
map.输入：水量 500ml。\n方案A 可利鲜（标准，ratio=1/500，1包1:
Input: water 500 ml.
Plan A Chrysal (standard, ratio=1/500, 1 packet 10g per 500 ml): amount = 500 × (1/500) = 1 g, about 0.1 standard packet (at 10g/packet), i.e. 1/10 of a packet per 500 ml.
Plan B homemade: per 500 ml water → white sugar 500/500 × 2 = 2 g + white vinegar 500/500 × 1 = 1 ml + bleach 500/500 × 0.5 = 0.5 ml.
Conclusion: for 500 ml vase water, commercial standard Chrysal takes about 1 g (or clear/Huazhishou at 1 packet 5g per 500 ml takes 5g); homemade can use 2 g sugar + 1 ml vinegar + 0.5 ml bleach, where sugar supplies energy and acid and bleach inhibit bacteria.
map.基础款（糖+弱酸+微量漂白剂）能短期延长花期，适合应急；但缺专业保鲜剂的乙烯抑制: The basic version (sugar + weak acid + trace bleach) can extend bloom life short-term and suits emergencies; but it lacks the ethylene inhibitor and chelating agent of professional preservatives, so it is weaker than commercial. Do not overuse sugar (rots stems), keep bleach truly trace (a few drops), and use unscented.
map.所有花都能用同比例吗？: Can all flowers use the same ratio?
map.木本（月季/绣球）可略多加糖促开放；敏感花（非洲菊/鸢尾）糖量宜低；水面以下叶要: Woody flowers (rose/hydrangea) can take slightly more sugar to promote opening; sensitive flowers (gerbera/iris) should use low sugar; remove all leaves below the waterline, re-cut stems 1-2 cm daily, and keep away from light with ventilation — these affect life more than the ratio alone.
